- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots and fails to cap upward momentum; reduce forecast peak by 1–2% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for momentum bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–5 days ahead); apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias for short-term lag.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.30 or more), model overfits to recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment < -0.50), model often fails to recognize structural support; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to avoid bottoming too early.
